items: Engagement: Corporate Positioning for {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}

Prepared by Daniel Valenzuela, Advisor
Drafting support: Michelle Rose, Communications Associate
Client lead: Mary Frank, Director of Operations

blocks.text: Where the Story Sits Today

items: The operating results are solid, but the outside story trails what the business actually does.
The language reads differently on the website, in recent releases, and in leadership remarks.
There is no single sentence an analyst or reporter would reach for to describe the company.
Two competitors have already claimed category language this business has a stronger right to.
The upside is real: the fundamentals support a sharper, more confident story than the one being told.

blocks.text: What We Heard at Kickoff

items: Leadership wants growth described as disciplined, not scale for its own sake.
The board does not want anything that reads as pre-IPO promotion.
Operations sees daylight between how the company runs and how it currently sounds.
Every external claim needs a fact behind it that your team can stand up on request.

blocks.text: The Frame We Are Building

items: One core positioning statement the whole company can repeat without adjustment.
A messaging map that pairs each audience with a single claim and the proof behind it.
An executive narrative so leaders tell the same story in the same order.
A plain-language replacement for the boilerplate that has aged out of use.
An announcement calendar ordered so each release reinforces the one before it.

blocks.text: How the First Weeks Run

items: We gather the current materials and mark every place the language diverges.
Michelle Rose turns the agreed direction into draft copy for your review.
Nothing investor-facing circulates until the internal narrative is settled.
You see each draft before it moves past the working group.
We hold one master copy of every document so your team is never reading an old version.

blocks.text: Next Step

items: Working group confirmed: Daniel Valenzuela and Michelle Rose here, Mary Frank leading on your side.
Send two or three windows this week for a thirty-minute walk-through of the draft messaging map, and I will set it up.

blocks.text: Discussion

The group met to review the positioning work at the midpoint of the engagement. Daniel Valenzuela walked through the core positioning statement, now settled, and the messaging map beneath it. Mary Frank confirmed the disciplined-growth framing matches how leadership at {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} wants the company described. The board's response to the earlier draft was positive.

Michelle Rose took the map claim by claim. Most proof points are confirmed against a source the company can produce on request. Two customer-outcome claims still lean on anecdote rather than a number, and the group agreed to soften both until the data is in hand. One figure on the operations side had been open; Mary Frank supplied it during the session, which closed the last gap in the growth-and-margin claim. The group agreed the map is complete for this phase. Attention now shifts to sequencing: aligning the executive narrative and ordering the announcement calendar behind the new frame.

On the executive narrative, the group reviewed how leadership would carry the statement in remarks and interviews. Daniel Valenzuela noted that the language works only if it is used the same way at every level, and proposed a short internal rollout note before anything external moves. Michelle Rose agreed to draft it. Mary Frank asked that the note be plain enough for staff to pick up without a briefing.

Daniel Valenzuela flagged one risk. With the statement settled, there is a pull to start using the new language externally before leadership has absorbed it. The group agreed no external message goes out until leadership signs off on the internal wording. Mary Frank asked that internal and external language stay in step as her team begins using the new terms day to day.

On the announcement calendar, the group sketched the order of the coming releases so each one builds on the last rather than competing with it. No dates were fixed; Daniel Valenzuela will bring a first cut of the sequence to the next session for the group to react to. Mary Frank noted two fixed points on the company's side that the calendar has to work around, and will send those so the draft sequence accounts for them.

On cadence, the group will keep the weekly status thread running and reconvene once the rollout note is reviewed. Mary Frank asked that interim decisions be confirmed in writing so the operations team is never guessing at the current version. Michelle Rose will hold the master copy of the map and date each change.
